title: Uganda to withdraw troops from DR Congo town after army chief's threat sparks row
summary: Uganda's army on Friday said it planned to withdraw from the eastern DR Congo town of Lubero in North Kivu. The announcement came days after Ugandan army chief Muhoozi Kainerugaba – son of President Yoweri Museveni – threatened to take control of Walikale, another North Kivu town, sparking a diplomatic spat between the two neighbouring nations.

title: Almost a million Americans left without power on Thanksgiving as storm sweeps East Coast
summary: Nearly a million people were left without power Thursday after a severe storm lashed the East Coast of the US, tearing up trees and powerlines on Thanksgiving. New York City authorities had been forced to postpone the annual Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade due to the intense winds.

title: France is dealing with water insecurity – a new study shows it's a global problem
summary: Tens of thousands of people in France are living under water restrictions as the country deals with a drought despite recent rains, according to the environment ministry. But this is a global problem, as a new study released Wednesday revealed "the largest global decline in surface water resources recorded" since 1991, when data collection began.

title: France and Germany push for EU budget deal by year-end as far-right rise threatens Ukraine aid
summary: As Europe braces itself for a slew of tense elections in 2027, Paris and Berlin are pushing for the European Union to strike a budget deal by December 31 to lock in financial aid for Ukraine. But Thursday's talks in Brussels seem to have done little to build consensus around the bloc's next budget.

title: Live: Trump calls on Putin to end all 'military aggression' against Europe
summary: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that he had urged his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to "pull back all military aggression against territories throughout Europe". Although Trump did not provide any further details, he added that he hoped this would pave the way for a peace deal to be struck between Kyiv and Moscow. Follow our liveblog for all the latest updates.

title: Spain’s Pedro makes final campaign push to beat the right ahead of crunch vote
summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez makes his final campaign push with a rally in Madrid Friday, the last day of campaigning for Sunday's high-stakes elections. Opinion polls show the Socialist premier lagging behind the main right-wing Popular Party (PP) as the Spanish vote opens an electoral cycle over the next 12 months that could reshape the balance of power within the EU.

title: With Spain’s far right on the cusp of power, can women bail Sanchez out once again?
summary: Spanish women’s refusal to surrender hard-won rights helped Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez clinch an unlikely victory in a snap election three years ago. As he gambles with another early vote on Sunday, his hopes of defying the odds rest on women again rallying to block the far right from governing Spain for the first time since Francisco Franco’s dictatorship.

title: Ukraine submits Black Sea ceasefire offer, awaits Russian response
summary: ⁠Ukraine ​made a Black Sea ceasefire offer ​to enable food exports and passed the details on to international allies, a senior Ukrainian official said Friday, adding that Kyiv was waiting for a response from Moscow. The announcement came a day after Russia attacked ​two foreign grain carriers near Ukraine's Black Sea port of Odesa, according to Ukrainian authorities.

title: Five people hospitalised as Levski Sofia and Marseille fans clash ahead of Europa League game
summary: Fighting broke out ahead of Thursday's Europa League match between Levski Sofia and Olympique Marseille, with five Bulgarian fans ending up in hospital. Local media reported a number of Levski fans performing Nazi salutes in the lead-up to the skirmish.

title: French far-left candidate Mélenchon demands ‘thorough overhaul’ of Germany ties
summary: Jean-Luc Mélenchon, leader of the hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) party, on Friday declared he was "hostile" to German economic liberalism and its dominance of the European Union. The septuagenarian presidential candidate in the 2027 race also warned that France could be drawn into unwanted conflict as Germany's growing military strength makes it a "target" for other countries.

title: S&P revises France's outlook from 'stable' to 'negative'
summary: Rating agency S&P revised France’s outlook to "negative" from "stable" on Friday, citing growing budget pressures as weak economic growth and higher interest costs make it harder to reduce the deficit.

title: 'From bad to catastrophic: Iran's justice system was already unfair for many decades'
summary: Amid war with the US and Israel, Iranian protesters continue to face death sentences following what Amnesty International describes as grossly unfair, torture-tainted trials. “The situation has changed from bad to catastrophic,” says Raha Bahreini, Iranian-Canadian human rights lawyer and Amnesty International's researcher on Iran. Bahreini discusses the aftermath of the January 2026 protests, the authorities' efforts to equate peaceful dissent with treason and espionage, and the extrajudicial killings of peaceful protesters. Amnesty International is calling for an international criminal justice mechanism, potentially a special tribunal. “There needs to be criminal accountability for these crimes against humanity.”

title: Is Spain 'nostalgic' for Franco? Would traditional right PP consider an alliance with far-right Vox?
summary: After eight years of socialist-led government, Spain is at a crossroads. Can Pedro Sánchez pull off another electoral comeback, or will the conservative Partido Popular make way for the far right into national government for the first time since the end of Franco's 40-year brutal reign? Just back from Madrid, Richard Werly, Europe correspondent for the Swiss daily Blick, joins Angela Diffley to examine the final days of campaigning and the generational divisions shaping Sunday’s snap elections. The youth are divided between the left and the far-right Vox party. Sánchez, nicknamed the “Teflon politician”, has campaigned heavily on housing and social issues. “We may see an outgoing prime minister performing better than expected,” says Werly.

title: Israel's Eisenkot agrees to coalition deal with left-wing Democrats
summary: Israel's former military chief Gadi Eisenkot on Thursday struck a coalition deal with Yair Golan's left-leaning Democrats, bringing the country's opposition closer to forming a government after no single bloc secured a majority in the October elections.

title: Turkey summons Georgian envoy after football fans' pro-Palestine protest sparks clashes
summary: Turkey summoned ​Georgia's ambassador on ​Friday over violence that broke out ​at ‌a Europa ⁠League match in Batumi ‌between the Turkish Besiktas ⁠and Israeli Hapoel Beer-Sheva teams, according to a foreign ministry source. Clashes erupted after Besiktas fans unfurled a pro-Palestinian banner during the match, sparking the diplomatic row.

title: Under a new flag, North Korea carves out identity as fully fledged nuclear state
summary: North Korea has modified its national flag as part of a constitutional amendment. The text also enshrined the country's status as a nuclear power and removed any reference to the "peaceful reunification" pursued by Kim Jong Un's predecessors. Meanwhile, the reclusive leader has been keen to demonstrate his desire to expand diplomatic ties with friendly nations. Yuka Royer speaks with Edward Howell of Oxford University to put these recent developments into context.

title: Paris Paloma tackles Greek mythology, generative AI in her second album 'The Fatal Flaw'
summary: Dheepthika Laurent chats with Paris Paloma on set ahead of her Paris concert. The UK singer-songwriter and guitarist is promoting her second album, "The Fatal Flaw", an ode to Greek mythology, art and feminism. She tells us why this album is more personal than her first record, "Cacophony".

title: Uganda to withdraw troops from DR Congo
summary: First, Uganda is heading for the exit in eastern DR Congo. Kampala has announced the withdrawal of its troops from a key town in North Kivu, as relations with Kinshasa deteriorate following provocative comments from Uganda's army chief. Then, pregnant women are struggling to cope with extreme heat, while health experts warn of growing risks for unborn babies, from dehydration to premature births. And, after seeking safety, opportunity and a better life, many migrants in South Africa now face hostility, violence and growing exclusion. As anti-immigration sentiment gains ground, the country's promise is fading for those who once saw it as a land of hope.

title: With new law, Iraq sees rise in child marriage, custody battles
summary: In January 2025, Iraq's parliament passed an amendment allowing families to place their household under religious law, governing all issues around marriage, divorce and inheritance. The new Ja'fari law, a Shiite law, came into force in October 2025. One year on, its consequences have been raising serious alarm, especially among women, who say they've seen a major rollback of their rights. FRANCE 24's Marie-Charlotte Roupie reports, with Josh Vardey.

title: Why is India so afraid of Pakistan's new Netflix series?
summary: PRESS REVIEW – Friday, November 27: Controversy brews as India asks Netflix to ban a Pakistani series from being broadcast in the country. Tensions have been high between the two nations since last year's terror attack in the Kashmir region. Also in the news: Taiwanese voters will head to the polls for all-important local elections overshadowed by the threat of Chinese claims to the island. Finally, forget schadenfreude – practicing "freudenfreude" is better for your health.

title: Immigration: South Africa no longer an El Dorado for foreigners
summary: South Africa was once a welcoming country; a refuge for those fleeing conflict and persecution. But for thousands of foreigners, the dream of a new life in South Africa is turning into more of a nightmare. Against a backdrop of unemployment and economic hardship, anti-immigration movements are gaining ground. Our correspondents report.

title: Japan's radical past: Retracing the far-left groups of the 1970s
summary: Our correspondents delve into the history of Japan's radical left in the 1970s. From the United Red Army to the Japanese Red Army, several movements turned to armed struggle and violent action. More than half a century on, our team met with two former militants.

title: Lyon held and Marseille pushed in mixed Europa League night for French clubs
summary: There were mixed fortunes for the French clubs in Thursday's Europa League action, as Marseille saw off Levski Sofia (1-0) in the only win of the night. Lyon were held at home by Lillestrom of Norway, while Rennes fell to Dutch side Nijmegen.

title: Spanish elections: 'Right-wing voters extremely mobilised, left-wing voters not mobilised enough'
summary: “His main political platform is to say, I am not Sánchez, I am the opposite of Sánchez.” As Spain heads to the polls, what do Alberto Núñez Feijóo's campaign and political career tell us about the kind of prime minister he might become? Javier Carbonell, Policy Analyst at the European Politics and Institutions Programme and lecturer at Sciences Po in Paris, joins Gavin Lee to break down the Popular Party leader's efforts to avoid the mistakes of 2023 and keep right-wing voters mobilised without galvanising the left.

title: 'Tribal loyalty' works on right: 'Heart on the left' sensitive to racism, anti-Semitism
summary: As French far-right leader Jordan Bardella denies fresh allegations concerning anti-Semitic remarks he allegedly made as a teenager, how much damage could the affair do to Marine Le Pen's presidential prospects? Ana Navarro Pedro, correspondent for Portuguese media, believes its electoral impact may be limited, despite Le Pen's defence of Bardella and her choice of him as a future prime minister. "What they most regret in this whole episode is that Bardella is denying it," she says of prospective Le Pen voters.

title: Big EU defence projects under threat from proposed budget cuts: Commissioner Andrius Kubilius
summary: We speak to the EU's Commissioner for Defence and Space, Andrius Kubilius. The former prime minister of Lithuania – who grew up during the Soviet era – tells us how he sees the confrontation between Europe and Russia. He also sounds the alarm over proposed cuts in the EU's future budget, saying that they could jeopardise major European projects in defence and space. Kubilius praises the EU's SAFE defence loans programme, remarking that it has been "really very successful".

title: From cyberbullying to extremist content, can EU Kids Act protect minors online?
summary: Almost every European teenager is online. Some 96 percent of 15-year-olds use social media, yet many say they do not feel safe there. One in four children in the EU, aged 12 to 17, report having experienced cyberbullying, and nearly one in three say social media has left them feeling stressed, sad or socially excluded.

title: The AI revolution: Will I lose my job?
summary: Have you heard of FOBO? It stands for fear of being obsolete. So as AI spreads, is it going to impact women in the workforce more than men? And are we right to be fearful of becoming obsolete? The International Labour Organization has already found occupations dominated by women are nearly twice as likely to be exposed to job losses thanks to generative AI, compared to those dominated by men.

title: The End of Spain’s ‘Frankenstein’ Coalition? Presidential Plotting in Paris, Kushner & Kremlin Trap
summary: Catch up with the World This Week with Gavin Lee. In just 45 minutes, make sense of seven extraordinary days in global affairs, as Gavin and his handpicked panel of four leading international correspondents unpack the stories shaping the world — and the questions behind the headlines. This week: Spain’s snap election; the presidential plotting unfolding over lunch at the Brasserie Concorde in Paris; Ukraine, Kushner and the ‘Kremlin Trap’; and the question hanging over Iran: whose side is time on? Joining Gavin are New World Magazine columnist Emma-Kate Symonds; Constant Méheut, The New York Times correspondent in Ukraine; Venetia Rainer, Daily Telegraph Foreign Editor and host of Iran: The Latest; and Sarah Morris, France 24’s correspondent in Spain.

title: Asia and Europe stocks rally after volatile week
summary: Stocks jumped on Wall Street on Friday, putting markets on track for strong weekly gains despite several days of erratic swings. Jameel Ahmad, Chief Analyst at GTC, tells us more.

title: Black Friday: How the global shopping phenomenon is evolving amid the cost-of-living crisis
summary: Online spending on Black Friday is expected to rise by 9.2% year-on-year to $12.9 billion, driven by increased use of Buy Now, Pay Later options and steep discounts on televisions, toys and furniture, according to Adobe's initial forecast. But with promotions now running throughout the year, are consumers experiencing deal fatigue? And how is the cost-of-living crisis shaping their shopping habits? We discuss these questions with Hilary Ingham, Head of Department and Professor of Economics at Lancaster University.

title: Black Friday: The evolution of a shopping phenomenon
summary: Once defined by crowds queuing outside shops for one-off bargains, Black Friday has evolved into weeks of online promotions. As discounts spread throughout the year, consumers are becoming more cautious about advertised deals, increasingly turning to AI and price comparisons to find genuine bargains. Camille Knight looks at the origins of the global shopping phenomenon.

title: Bulgarian fans injured after clashes between supporters at Marseille-Levski game in Europa League
summary: French and Bulgarian authorities condemned the violence that left at least 11 Bulgarian soccer fans injured during clashes between Marseille and Levski Sofia supporters before their Europa League match on Thursday evening, and Marseille prosecutors opened two investigations.

title: DR Congo: Copper reserves put Africa at the centre of the global race for critical minerals
summary: Africa is emerging as a key player in the global race for copper, accounting for around 10 per cent of the world's estimated reserves. The Democratic Republic of Congo is at the centre of this growing interest, having mined 3.4 million metric tons of copper in 2025. Its vast mineral resources are attracting growing attention from countries and companies around the world, as demand for the metal rises due to its importance in energy infrastructure, electric vehicles and the global transition to cleaner energy.

title: EU: Leaders fail to reach agreement on next budget after tense summit
summary: At the bloc headquarters in Brussels on Thursday, EU leaders failed to reach a consensus after more than 12 hours of talks over the budget and a new $49 billion loan for Ukraine’s economic and military needs next year. France 24's Dave Keating tells us more.

title: EU leaders split over budget spending and a $49 billion loan to Ukraine
summary: French President Emmanuel Macron set an end-of-year deadline for an agreement on the European Union's next seven-year budget after the continent's leaders ruled out any chances for a deal to be reached at their summit on Thursday.

title: France: David Lisnard shakes up presidential race
summary: David Lisnard, the mayor of Cannes and a candidate in France's 2027 presidential election, has climbed to third place in several opinion polls. His rise is shaking up the political landscape on the right and centre. We discuss what this means with France 24's James André.

title: France: Macron lashes out at Le Pen’s ‘arrogance’
summary: 🇫🇷 French President Emmanuel #Macron on Thursday responded to far-right leader and 2027 presidential candidate Marine #LePen’s claim that he was “blocking” the French people’s freedom of expression. Listen in to what he had to say.

title: Israel's Eisenkot and left-wing party agree coalition deal
summary: The centrist party of Gadi Eisenkot, who is trying to form the next Israeli government, and an allied left-wing party on Thursday announced they had agreed on a coalition deal.

title: Israel's Eisenkot reaches deal with left-wing faction as coalition talks gain steam
summary: Gadi ​Eisenkot's Yashar party and a left-wing faction agreed on a preliminary coalition deal on Thursday, after a brief dispute that had posed a challenge to his bid to unseat Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu following an inconclusive election last month. France 24's Andrew Hilliar tells us more.

title: Kuwait: Two Italians killed in drone attack
summary: A drone attack in Kuwait killed two Italian technicians working on an air defence system on Thursday, marking the first fatal strike in the Gulf state for months.

title: Nigeria: Political violence and attacks on candidates raise fears ahead of January elections
summary: Political violence is escalating in Nigeria ahead of the general elections scheduled for January. Candidates and their supporters have increasingly come under attack, with armed groups disrupting campaign rallies and some assaults resulting in deaths. Despite the growing number of incidents, security forces have struggled to contain the violence. With less than two months to go before the vote, fears are mounting that intimidation and deadly attacks could prevent many Nigerians from freely taking part in the democratic process.

title: OM - Levski Sofia: A night of violence disrupts Marseille match
summary: 🇫🇷 ⚽ 🇧🇬 At least 11 supporters of Bulgarian football club #LevskiSofia were injured in Marseille on Thursday, as skirmishes broke out between the visiting club and fans of hosts Olympique Marseille (#OM) before their Europa League fixture, FRANCE 24 has the details.

title: Sierra Leone: Maternal deaths fall as healthcare improves, but challenges remain
summary: Sierra Leone was once considered one of the most dangerous countries in the world to give birth. Maternal deaths have since fallen dramatically, thanks to improvements in healthcare, medical training and maternity services. But despite this progress, significant challenges remain. Activists warn that continued efforts are needed to ensure safer pregnancies and childbirth for women across the country. Clarisse Fortuné reports.

title: Spain election: Housing crisis and immigration dominate final campaign debate
summary: Spain goes to the polls on Sunday in an early parliamentary election that may usher in a right-wing coalition to replace the Socialist-led minority government of Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, one of Europe's last leftist leaders. Our correspondent Sarah Morris tells us more.

title: Spain general election 2026: Could Sánchez lose power?
summary: Spanish voters head to the polls in just three days for a snap election, after eight years of Socialist-led rule. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez is fighting to stay in power, but an alliance between the conservative People's Party and the far-right VOX could bring his time in office to an end. So what are the key issues, and what's at stake?

title: Spain races to stop oil spill after ship capsizes off Ibiza
summary: Spanish authorities raced to contain any damage to ecologically valuable Mediterranean waters on Thursday after a tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes of diesel capsized off Ibiza, leaving one dead.

title: French student protests: A 'very bizarre' government response
summary: “The government had a very bizarre way of dealing with the student protests,” says Jean-Rémi Girard, a secondary school teacher and union representative in Asnières-sur-Seine. He explains how teachers sought to defuse tensions by listening to students, and respecting their right to protest, while keeping classes running. He recounts a police intervention last October and the case of a student facing trial for defending a classmate, and has the full support of several teachers. Girard questions the government's heavy-handed policing and largely symbolic proposals on class sizes and university admissions. “There wasn't really a negotiation,” he says, also highlighting the number of education workers injured during the protests.

title: Ukraine: How much have Europeans spent on aid?
summary: Since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022, EU member states have provided around €200 billion in aid to Ukraine, making them its largest contributors ahead of the United States. Germany leads in total financial contributions, with around €54 billion, roughly twice France's €27 billion. But the picture changes when aid is measured against GDP or per capita, with Denmark and other Nordic countries ranking among the biggest contributors.

title: Ukraine: Residents brace for another difficult winter
summary: As Russia continues to target Ukraine's energy infrastructure, residents are preparing for another difficult winter of strikes and power cuts. With supply chains under pressure, food prices are also rising, forcing many Ukrainians to cut back on essentials or stock up ahead of the coming months.

title: US: Thanksgiving storms cause flooding and travel chaos
summary: Severe storms battered the US East Coast on Thursday, bringing torrential rain, strong winds and coastal flooding. Nearly one million homes were left without power, while hundreds of flights were cancelled and thousands delayed during one of the country's busiest travel periods. The weather also forced the postponement of New York's Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade until Saturday.
